record.paper_title: The True Prosoluble Completion of a Group: Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let G be a complete Hausdorff topological group such that every nonidentity element g in G is omitted by some open normal subgroup N of G with soluble quotient G/N. Find useful characterizations of when such a topological group G is isomorphic to the true prosoluble completion PS(Gamma) of a residually soluble discrete group Gamma. In particular, how can one decide whether G is isomorphic to PS(Gamma) for some finitely generated Gamma, and how can one decide whether G is isomorphic to PS(Gamma) for some finitely presented Gamma?

evidence.quote: (iii) Can one find interesting characterizations of those groups which are true prosoluble completions of residually soluble group? More precisely, let G be a complete Hausdorff topological group such that, for any g ∈ G, g 6= 1, there exists an open normal subgroup N of G not containing g such that G/N is soluble; how can it be decided whether G is isomorphic to P S(Γ) for some finitely generated group Γ? for some finitely presented group Γ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the true prosoluble completion of a residually soluble discrete group Γ as the inverse limit
  PS(Γ) = lim_{←} Γ/N,
taken over the directed system of all normal subgroups N of Γ such that Γ/N is a soluble group, endowed with the natural profinite-style topology making it a complete Hausdorff topological group in which every nonidentity element is separated from 1 by an open normal subgroup with soluble quotient.

Call a complete Hausdorff topological group G "prosoluble-Hausdorff" if for every g ∈ G with g ≠ 1 there exists an open normal subgroup N ◁ G with g ∉ N and such that G/N is a (discrete) soluble group.

Problem. Find useful intrinsic characterizations of those prosoluble-Hausdorff topological groups G that arise as true prosoluble completions of residually soluble discrete groups. Specifically:

(a) Give a criterion, formulated intrinsically in terms of G, deciding whether there exists a finitely generated residually soluble group Γ such that G ≅ PS(Γ) as topological groups.

(b) Give a criterion, formulated intrinsically in terms of G, deciding whether there exists a finitely presented residually soluble group Γ such that G ≅ PS(Γ) as topological groups.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on true prosoluble completions of residually soluble groups. No subsequent work found in the search resolves the intrinsic characterization of which complete Hausdorff prosoluble-type topological groups arise as PS(Γ) for finitely generated or finitely presented Γ; related work focuses on examples, on the soluble/finite genus problem for free and surface groups, and on residual properties, but does not provide the requested characterization.

status_evidence.title: The true prosoluble completion of a group: examples and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists characterization of true prosoluble completions among prosoluble-type Hausdorff groups as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization question for PS(Γ) is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The finite and solvable genus of finitely generated free and surface groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies solvable genus (groups sharing soluble quotients) but does not provide an intrinsic characterization of PS(Γ).
status_evidence.claim: Recent related work addresses solvable genus rather than the intrinsic characterization sought.
